title: ESP32, from the bench to the fridge
blurb: The microcontroller behind most home devices: the chips, GPIO and power, MicroPython, sensors on I²C and 1-Wire, Wi-Fi and MQTT, deep sleep, ESPHome, and a fridge probe that reports to the house.
lede: From a bare dev board to a device in the house: MicroPython first, ESPHome for the ones that stay, MQTT into the leaf on jarvis.

shift.label: The one big mental shift
shift.html:
There's no operating system to catch you. Your program is the device: if it hangs, the device hangs; if it runs out of memory after three days, it resets; if the voltage dips when Wi-Fi starts, it reboots and looks like a software bug.

So for every device, ask: what happens when the network, the sensor or the power misbehaves? How does it recover with nobody there? And how will you find out it did?

plan_foot: When you finish a day, leave the board running overnight doing that day's thing, and check in the morning that it still is.

items.t: Order the kit
items.why: Two ESP32-C3 or S3 dev boards (one will die), a breadboard and jumper wires, a waterproof DS18B20 probe, 4.7 kΩ and 220 Ω resistors, a few LEDs and buttons, a USB cable you know carries data, and a USB power meter.

items.t: Chip, module, dev board; and which ESP32 is which
items.why: Original: dual-core, most quirks. S3: native USB, often PSRAM. C3: small RISC-V. C6: adds Zigbee/Thread. H2: no Wi-Fi. Almost all 2.4 GHz only.

items.t: Flash MicroPython with esptool
items.why: Erase, then write the firmware for your exact chip at the offset its download page gives. Can't connect: hold BOOT, tap RESET, release BOOT.
src: MicroPython: getting started on the ESP32

items.t: The REPL and files with mpremote
items.why: mpremote, mpremote cp main.py :, mpremote run test.py. boot.py then main.py at power-up; develop with run.

items.t: GPIO in and out, pull-ups, a resistor on every LED
items.why: 3.3 V, not 5 V tolerant, a few mA per pin. A floating input reads noise: use Pin.PULL_UP.

items.t: Interrupts and debounce
items.why: The handler sets a flag; the main loop does the work. Ignore edges within ~50 ms.

items.t: Pins to avoid: flash, strapping, input-only, ADC2
items.why: Original ESP32: 6–11 flash, 0/2/5/12/15 strapping, 34–39 input only, ADC2 dead with Wi-Fi. Check your board's own list.

items.t: Power: peaks, brownouts, a shared ground
items.why: Wi-Fi peaks at hundreds of mA. Resets when Wi-Fi starts are usually the supply. Every device needs a common ground.

checks.t: I can get from a fresh board to a REPL, including when esptool can't connect
I can wire a button with the internal pull-up and say why it reads 0 when pressed
I can explain a reset that happens only when Wi-Fi starts

items.t: A device program: a loop that catches, logs and never ends
items.why: Timeouts on everything that can hang. ticks_diff, never subtraction.

items.t: Memory: allocate once, nothing that grows
items.why: gc.mem_free() stable over an hour is the test. A growing list ends in MemoryError days later.

items.t: I²C: scan first
items.why: i2c.scan() empty means wiring or power, not the driver. A BME280 is 0x76 or 0x77.

items.t: The DS18B20: 4.7 kΩ pull-up, 750 ms, and 85 °C means it failed
items.why: convert_temp, wait, read_temp per rom. Throw away the first reading and range-check.

items.t: ADC and PWM, with their limits
items.why: 11 dB attenuation, read_uv, average; not better than a few percent. PWM duty for LEDs and fans; a MOSFET for anything big.

items.t: Join Wi-Fi with a timeout
items.why: A board that waits forever for a rebooting router needs unplugging. Passwords in secrets.py, not git.

items.t: umqtt: client ID from machine.unique_id(), a retained will, ping within keepalive
items.why: umqtt.simple doesn't ping or reconnect for you.

items.t: The recover loop: Wi-Fi, connect, work; on error back off and start over
items.why: The same loop as aiomqtt's in the MQTT course. mqtt_as does it for asyncio programs.

items.t: Build one: the DS18B20 publishing to a broker on the Mac
items.why: Retained readings with a timestamp, on change or every 5 min, a will and birth. Restart the broker and check it comes back.

checks.t: I can say what a DS18B20 reading of 85.0 means
I can write the Wi-Fi + MQTT recover loop from memory
I can say why time.ticks_ms() - start is a bug

items.t: Deep sleep is a reset: main.py runs once per wake
items.why: RTC memory for a few bytes across sleeps. Wi-Fi is where the battery goes: send rarely.

items.t: ESPHome: the fridge sensor as YAML, with OTA
items.why: esphome run fridge.yaml. USB once, then over Wi-Fi. MQTT so the house's programs see it.

items.t: A watchdog, fed only from the main loop
items.why: Never from a timer. Publish the reset cause at boot so you hear about watchdog resets.

items.t: NTP after every boot; no timestamps before it
items.why: The clock starts at 2000 after a power cut.

items.t: Build the fridge probe end to end
items.why: Device to the leaf on jarvis as its own MQTT user, a watcher subscribed over NATS, notify.anish to Friday. Run the five "done means" tests.

items.t: Put the firmware in git, secrets out
items.why: YAML or .py files in a repo (a devices/ folder under home/ fits the projects map); secrets.yaml and secrets.py gitignored.

checks.t: I can say why a sleeping device's last will doesn't mean much, and what to use instead
I can say why the door alert belongs off the device
The probe has survived a router restart and a jarvis restart without me touching it
